text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV cache paged metadata growth detected in us-east-1. Continuous batching spike causing block metadata count to climb rapidly, memory pressure on runtime nodes, tail latency rising. Auto-scaling attempted but lagging. Please acknowledge and triage. thread_ts=2359879999

Tina Huang: ack i'm oncall, jumping in. first things: can we get blockmgr stats and which pools/nodes are hot?

Samir Shah: pulling stats now — internal /admin/blockmgr endpoint. here's a quick scrape:

```
# curl http://rt-us-east-1-admin.internal/blockmgr/stats
block_metadata_count: 1,042,112
block_metadata_bytes: 2.1GB
active_batchers: 48
avg_batch_size_tokens: 2,750
max_batch_size_tokens: 8192
eviction_policy: LRU
```

Samir Shah: note the avg_batch_size_tokens is way up compared to baseline (~512). looks like a traffic pattern changed and continuous batching is coalescing very large prefixes.

Alex Rodriguez: probable root is the recent rollout of the dynamic-batching heuristic (deployed 18h ago) — it increased max_batch_tokens for certain routes. propose immediate mitigation: reduce max_batch_tokens and increase eviction aggressiveness for paged KV blockmgr.

Chris Patel: +1 to config change. prefer in-place config flip rather than node restarts. we can do canary shutdown of the largest batch pools first (drain traffic) then apply config. avoid mass restart because canaries running inference for paying customers.

Tina Huang: plan: 1) scale down/shore up canary pools -> drain the highest-batch containers 2) update runtime config: `max_batch_tokens: 8192 -> 2048`, `eviction_target_ratio: 0.6 -> 0.4`, `block_size_bytes: 8MB -> 4MB` 3) watch metrics for 10m, if backend latency drops, roll to remaining pools.

Samir Shah: commands to flip config via admin API (run from ops bastion):

```
# mark: reduce batching and make eviction more aggressive
curl -X POST 'https://control-plane.internal/runtime/config' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"scope":"us-east-1","runtime_overrides": {"max_batch_tokens": 2048, "eviction_target_ratio": 0.4, "block_size_bytes": 4194304}}'
```

Samir Shah: also applying a temporary key-value to force block metadata scrub interval shorter: `metadata_prune_interval_sec: 300` (was 1800).

Alex Rodriguez: i'll coordinate the canary drain. oncall-bot, can you take the first canary down and route its traffic to spare nodes?

oncall-bot: executing canary drain on pool rt-canary-3 in us-east-1. ETA ~90s. :gear:

oncall-bot: canary drain completed. pool now at 0 active requests.

Chris Patel: applying config change to us-east-1 control plane now.

```
# patch applied
PATCH /runtime/config/us-east-1 200 OK
{"applied": true, "changes": {"max_batch_tokens":2048,"eviction_target_ratio":0.4,"block_size_bytes":4194304}}
```

Tina Huang: i'm watching blockmgr metrics. initial diff:

```
pre-change block_metadata_count: 1,042,112
1m after change: 1,015,824
5m after change: 998,400
tail latency (p99) pre: 420ms -> now: 160ms
mem pressure on nodes down ~30%
```

Samir Shah: looks promising. also saw a noisy task that wasn't expiring block metadata properly — log excerpt: `WARN blockmgr: metadata orphaned for 00:12:34, candidate cleanup failed: tombstone missing` — i suspect a metadata leak on certain delete paths.

Alex Rodriguez: open follow-up: need deep dive on metadata lifecycle — that will be a separate bugfix. For now, config change + shorter prune interval reduced the buildup.

Chris Patel: customer impact: CS reported elevated latency for a small set of enterprise customers on us-east-1 for about 18m. Maria C-S, can you ping affected accounts and let them know we mitigated and are doing a root-cause follow-up?

Maria C-S: on it. message drafted: "we saw temporary increased latency due to internal batching heuristic; mitigation applied and latency normalized. engineering will follow up with a detailed postmortem and timeline." will send now. :email:

Tina Huang: rolling to remaining pools in 2m to ensure stability. monitoring for signs of regression (block_metadata_count rising again).

Samir Shah: logging note for postmortem: the sequence is batching rollout -> sustained large prefixes -> blockmgr metadata growth -> eviction lag -> tail latency. Also include `continuous_batching.enabled=true` metric spikes.

Chris Patel: I've pinned the temporary config change for 6 hours; we'll revert to a safer tuned value after the metadata leak is fixed. also created a short-term alert: "block_metadata_count > 900k for 5m" to prevent slow buildup.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied, latency reduced to baseline, customers notified. severity lowered to SEV-3.

Tina Huang: handing off to next oncall in 2h — please own monitoring and the follow-ups: 1) dig into metadata leak (lib/blockmgr delete path) 2) evaluate whether dynamic-batching heuristic needs a guardrail (max_batch_tokens per route) 3) improve observability: add per-route batch size histograms 4) create runbook step for canary drain + apply-config.

Alex Rodriguez: i'll take the metadata leak owner. Samir can own observability items. Chris will coordinate with infra to make the alert permanent.

Samir Shah: short term mitigation ticket created: INFRA-PT-4321. assign to eng-runtime.

Maria C-S: CS update sent. one customer already replied: "thanks for the quick response, please keep us posted."

Tina Huang: thanks team. if nothing else, i'll close this thread when handed off. leaving detailed timestamps and changed keys in the incident log. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: handing off to next-oncall: @alex rodriguez at 2359880699.

Alex Rodriguez: ack, taking over monitoring and follow-ups. adding to my calendar for tomorrow: deep-dive triage.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated) — root cause investigation required.
